What Are Colorado’s Insurance Requirements?
All motor vehicle operators in Colorado, including motorcyclists, must maintain the required amounts of insurance under state law. Currently, these amounts are:
$25,000 in bodily injury or death liability insurance per person
$50,000 in bodily injury or death insurance per accident
$15,000 in property damage liability insurance
Operating any type of vehicle with less than these amounts – or no insurance at all – is against the law. Unfortunately, many motorcyclists and others in Colorado break this law every day.
Is Colorado a Fault or No-Fault Insurance State?

Colorado uses a fault-based system to determine financial responsibility, or liability, in a car accident case. If you get into an accident, the person who is most at fault for causing the collision will be liable for your medical bills and property damage. If you caused the crash, for example, you would use your own car insurance coverage to pay for the injured motorcyclist’s bills. If the motorcyclist caused the crash, however, he or she will be responsible for paying – typically through his or her insurance.
How to Recover if the At-Fault Party Doesn’t Have Insurance

If a motorcyclist was unlawfully riding while uninsured or underinsured, you may have to seek financial compensation from your own insurance company instead. Call your own car insurance provider after this type of accident and ask if you have uninsured or underinsured motorist insurance. This specific type of coverage will pay for your losses and damages after getting into a collision with an uninsured motorcyclist. It is an optional type of coverage in Colorado, however, that may not be part of your policy. If you don’t have this type of insurance, work with an attorney to examine your other options, such as holding a party other than the motorcyclist financially responsible.
What to Do After an Accident Involving an Uninsured or Underinsured Motorcyclist

Do not admit fault or apologize for an accident involving a motorcyclist, even if the rider suffered more severe injuries in the crash than you did. As soon as you find out that the motorcyclist does not have automobile insurance, contact the police to report the collision. The police can document the crash with an official accident report, as well as punish the motorcyclist for unlawfully driving while uninsured or underinsured. Request your police report number before you go.

Visit a hospital in Denver without delay to receive professional medical care for any injuries that you suffered in the accident. Keep copies of your medical records and bills for your insurance claim later. Once you are on the mend, call your own car insurance company to report the wreck.

Explain that the motorcyclist involved in the collision does not have insurance. Be careful when speaking to an insurance claims adjuster about your accident, even if it is your own insurance provider. The insurance company may try to take advantage of you to protect its profits. Before accepting a settlement for your accident, discuss all of your legal options with a
Denver personal injury lawyer.
What Are Your Options if the Motorcyclist Doesn’t Have Insurance?

Although you will not have the motorcyclist’s auto insurance available to pay for your expenses, there may be other options that can help you pay for your property repairs, medical bills, lost wages and other expenses:

Collecting compensation from your own insurance company. If you have uninsured or underinsured motorist insurance, this will pay for your property damage and other losses after a crash involving a motorcyclist who does not have insurance. This is an optional type of car insurance in Colorado, however, that you may not have.

Filing a claim or lawsuit against a third party. Without the correct type of first-party insurance, your other option is to bring a claim against a third party other than the uninsured motorcyclist. For example, you may have grounds to bring a claim against the government for a road hazard that contributed to the wreck.

Holding the uninsured/underinsured motorist liable. There is a high likelihood that a motorcyclist who does not have insurance also cannot pay for a settlement out of pocket. However, an attorney can investigate this option for you. If the motorcyclist does have the funds or assets available, holding him or her personally responsible could be an option for financial recovery.
